title: Timeline
intro_md: The eras, the firsts, the releases and the milestones, oldest first. Dates are US Eastern.

items.label: 14 Oct 2004
items.title: ares's lineage begins
items.detail_md: The line ares descends from begins: bsnes, then higan, then ares.

items.label: 25 Jul 2026
items.title: Phobos forks ares
items.detail_md: From ares's commit of that day, to take it to Android.

items.label: 27 Jul 2026
items.title: Phobos runs on Android
items.detail_md: The 64-bit native Android app, and native Vulkan for the N64 core, the same day.

items.label: 20 Aug 2026
items.title: v1.0.0
items.detail_md: The Neo Geo core, the GPU Driver Manager, stable release signing, the PC Engine and SuperGrafx.

items.label: 15 Sep
items.title: A change process with evidence
items.detail_md: Speed claims need measurements; every change needs an independent review before it merges.

items.label: 24 Sep
items.title: The first pull request merged
items.detail_md: Neo Geo CD's garbled menu text: a DMA's byte order (#1).

items.label: 25-28 Sep
items.title: The N64 speed push
items.detail_md: Linked JIT blocks (#10), NEON in the RSP (#15, #16), 256 parallel-RDP contexts (#17), WFE instead of spinning (#18).

items.label: 27-28 Sep
items.title: The app's look
items.detail_md: 37 themes with Retrowave effects (#9), the performance overlay (#5), glass panels and a floating dock (#20).

items.label: 28 Sep
items.title: v1.1.0
items.detail_md: Pull requests #1 to #25: the N64 work, the overlay, the themes, frontends that start games.

items.label: 28 Sep
items.title: In-app updates
items.detail_md: Phobos updates itself from GitHub's releases, every build numbered from git history (#26).

items.label: 29 Sep
items.title: A PSP core goes on the plan
items.detail_md: To rival PPSSPP in compatibility and speed.

items.label: 30 Sep
items.title: Controllers drive the menus
items.detail_md: The D-pad and stick move a visible focus; L1 and R1 switch tabs (#51).

items.label: 3 Oct
items.title: Back on the desktop
items.detail_md: A Linux AppImage, a universal macOS app and a Windows Phobos.exe (#97); Phobos's own code under GPL-3.0-or-later (#98).

items.label: 3 Oct
items.title: The PSP core's first code
items.detail_md: The Allegrex interpreter and recompiler, and the first measurement on a real PSP.

items.label: 5 Oct
items.title: The PSP in the app at 60 fps
items.detail_md: The PSP SDK's samples on the Retroid Pocket 6; on the host, the first retail title screens: Lumines and Street Fighter III 3rd Strike.

items.label: 6 Oct
items.title: Full speed on the device, and all 266 games run
items.detail_md: Peace Walker, Liberty City Stories and Lumines at full speed on the RP6; the headless runner's first pass over the library (#154, merged into the PSP stack just after midnight).

items.label: 7 Oct
items.title: The PSP drawn on the GPU
items.detail_md: A hardware renderer on Vulkan.

items.label: 11 Oct
items.title: v2.0.0, the first release with the PSP
items.detail_md: The PSP core, Experimental, merged as one stack of about 100 pull requests (#208).

items.label: 12 Oct
items.title: v2.1.0
items.detail_md: Fixes from playing v2.0.0 on the RP6; the PSP's system dialogs as the app's own (#221).

items.label: 13 Oct
items.title: v2.2.0
items.detail_md: The slow games' first rounds; Vulkan no longer waits for its own pixels.

items.label: 14 Oct
items.title: v2.3.0
items.detail_md: Savedata, sceFont, God Eater 2, CPU round 2, and the test plan's CI lanes.

items.label: 14 Oct
items.title: Measured on the device before merging
items.detail_md: The headless runner built for Android, so a commit is measured on the RP6 first (#255).

items.label: 15-16 Oct
items.title: The whole library at 5x on the RP6
items.detail_md: No crashes in 266 games; 232 averaged 59 fps or more.

items.label: 16 Oct
items.title: v2.4.0
items.detail_md: Polling loops skipped where exact, Vulkan depth and stencil, the runner on Android, EDATA and PGD on the memory stick.

items.label: 16 Oct
items.title: A real PSP times games' display lists
items.detail_md: A GE profiler on a PSP-1000: 4 to 12 times the old model's time.

items.label: 18 Oct
items.title: The GE on a thread of its own
items.detail_md: Exact, off by default (#272); and screenshots that hop into a folder (#273).

items.label: 19 Oct
items.title: A PSP's own timing becomes the default
items.detail_md: The GE takes about the time a PSP-1000 took; "Fast" is the opt-in (#269).

items.label: 20 Oct
items.title: The frame shown from the GE thread
items.detail_md: #277; and the N64 recompiler fixed on x86-64 desktops (#290).

items.label: 21 Oct
items.title: N64 on the stock Qualcomm driver
items.detail_md: No more black picture on the RP6's own driver (#292); Super Monkey Ball within 15% of the PSP (#291).
